nd1f99920ca6.s: The Ministry of Law and Justice, the oldest organ of the Government of India, traces its origin to the:
nd1f99920ca6.x: The Ministry traces its origin to the Charter Act of 1833, which introduced the Law Member and the first Law Commission.

n96e05d32c1d.s: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly in India but retained its exclusive trade in:
o: Spices, and trade with the East Indies
n96e05d32c1d.x: The 1813 Act ended the general monopoly in India but kept the Company's exclusive trade in tea and with China.

ndc3e8b59576.s: Which Act abolished the Directors' patronage and introduced open competition for civil-service recruitment?
ndc3e8b59576.x: The Charter Act of 1853 abolished the patronage of the Court of Directors and introduced open competition for civil-service recruitment.

n5f586d123fd.s: Who was the first Law Member (the fourth member) of the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1833?
n5f586d123fd.x: The 1833 Act added a Law Member as the fourth member of the Council; T. B. Macaulay was the first to hold the post.

nf0dc0051206.s: Which of the following is correct about the Charter Act of 1833?
o: It was the final step towards centralisation and made the Company purely administrative.
It abolished the Governor-General's office without creating a successor.
It was the first Charter Act to renew the Company's authority for a fixed 20-year term.
It restored the law-making powers of the presidencies.
nf0dc0051206.x: The Charter Act of 1833 is regarded as the final step towards centralisation and converted the Company into a purely administrative body.

nindian-history-131-19.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nindian-history-131-19.x: The Regulating Act was passed in 1773; Pitt's India Act was 1784, the Charter Act 1813 and the Government of India Act 1858.

n1bc13d46d60.s: The territory separated from the Bengal Presidency and placed under the Agra Presidency by the Charter Act of 1833 was renamed in 1836 as the:
n1bc13d46d60.x: The separated territory was placed under the Agra Presidency in 1834 and renamed the North-Western Provinces in 1836.

n2d17018d27a.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Raja Ram Mohan Roy – demand for Indian participation in services, 1853
Charter Act of 1813 – open competitive examination for the ICS
Fort William College – established by Wellesley, 1806
n2d17018d27a.x: Haileybury replaced Fort William College in 1806. Fort William College was set up in 1800, Roy's demand came in 1832 and open examinations came with the Charter Act of 1853.

nbab7c3e2c20.s: Under the Mahalwari system, the unit of revenue assessment was the:
nbab7c3e2c20.x: Under Mahalwari the mahal (village or estate) was the unit; revenue fixed for it was collected through the headman or village community.

nindian-history-110-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Permanent Settlement?
o: It covered Bengal, Bihar, Odisha and Varanasi.
It was associated with Lord Cornwallis.
Zamindars were recognised as proprietors of the land.
It was introduced in Madras and Coorg.
nindian-history-110-2.x: Madras and Coorg came under Ryotwari, not the Permanent Settlement.

nindian-history-110-14.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the first Ryotwari experiment?
o: Alexander Read was assisted by Munro.
The initial demand was 30% of the estimated produce.
nindian-history-110-14.x: The first Ryotwari demand was 50% of the estimated produce, not 30%.

nindian-history-110-18.s: Which of the following pairs (settlement – approximate share of British-held area) is correctly matched?
nindian-history-110-18.x: The Permanent Settlement covered about 19%, Ryotwari about 51% and Mahalwari about 30%, so Ryotwari and Mahalwari together covered about 81%.

nc7f3079892e.s: The Madras Inam Commission, which investigated titles to rent-free inam lands, was constituted in:
nc7f3079892e.x: The Madras Inam Commission was constituted in 1858 to investigate rent-free inam titles.

ncef7811e8ab.s: Which of the following correctly describes the land-revenue pattern in Andhra?
o: Ryotwari in the Circars, Zamindari in the Ceded Districts and Mahalwari in Nellore
Mahalwari in the Circars, Zamindari in Rayalaseema and Ryotwari in Nellore
Ryotwari in the Circars, Mahalwari in Rayalaseema and Zamindari in Nellore
Zamindari in the Circars, Ryotwari in the Ceded Districts and Mahalwari in Nellore
ncef7811e8ab.x: The Andhra pattern was Zamindari in the Circars, Ryotwari in the Ceded Districts and a Mahalwari-type arrangement in Nellore.

nceca1298e4b.s: Who was the first Principal Collector of Rayalaseema and established a direct ryot–state relationship there?
nceca1298e4b.x: Thomas Munro was the first Principal Collector of Rayalaseema and established the direct ryot–state relationship through ryotwari.

n03a01269abb.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: R.M. Bird – devised the Mahalwari system
James Thomason – revised the system through a survey-based settlement
Holt Mackenzie – carried on Bird's settlement in the NWP
Holt Mackenzie – devised the Mahalwari system
n03a01269abb.x: Holt Mackenzie devised the Mahalwari system; R.M. Bird revised it through survey-based settlement and James Thomason carried on Bird's settlement.

nacbcf7e1ee0.s: Which of the following pairs (place – product) is correctly matched?
nacbcf7e1ee0.x: Srikakulam was known for muslin; Machilipatnam for dyed clothes, Nellore for towels and Eluru for carpets.

nc9d53465b3d.s: Which of the following pairs (crop – main region) is correctly matched?
nc9d53465b3d.x: Jute was grown mainly in Bengal; cotton in the Deccan, Gujarat and Berar, opium in Bengal-Bihar and Malwa, and tea in Assam.

n7e46526cc19.s:
Consider the following statements about the Great Madras Famine of 1876–78:
1. Laissez-faire relief aggravated the famine.
2. Missionary John Clough's canal project was a notable relief effort.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
n7e46526cc19.x: Both are correct: laissez-faire relief worsened the famine, and John Clough's canal relief project was a notable response.

n5bc0666bb63.s: Which of the following pairs (Famine Commission – Viceroy) is correctly matched?
n5bc0666bb63.x: The Strachey Commission belongs to Lytton's time; Campbell was under John Lawrence, Lyall under Elgin II and MacDonnell under Curzon.

n010cdc92874.s: Which famine of 1833 gave the impetus for Cotton's Godavari anicut?
n010cdc92874.x: The Guntur famine of 1833 led to the construction of Cotton's Godavari anicut.

na323783aee7.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Madras University
2. Central Collegiate Institute
3. Noble School
4. Result-based grants-in-aid system
na323783aee7.x: Central Collegiate Institute (1841), Noble School (1843), Madras University (1857) and result-based grants-in-aid (1877–78).

nindian-history-14-5.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindu College was established in Calcutta in 1817.
2. Delhi College was established in Delhi in 1824.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
nindian-history-14-5.x: Both are correct: Hindu College, Calcutta dates from 1817 and Delhi College from 1824.

nindian-history-14-7.s: Which of the following pairs (institution – founder/associated person) is correctly matched?
nindian-history-14-7.x: Jonathan Duncan founded the Sanskrit College, Banaras; Warren Hastings founded the Calcutta Madarsa, Mayo College is named after Richard Bourke (Lord Mayo) and Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu School.

nindian-history-14-23.s:
Consider the following statements about the Calcutta Madarsa:
1. It was set up by Warren Hastings.
2. It was established in 1780.
3. It was the first Madarsa set up by the British in India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
nindian-history-14-23.x: All three are correct: Warren Hastings set up the Calcutta Madarsa in 1780, the first Madarsa established by the British in India.

nap-history-32-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly dated?
nap-history-32-2.x: Osmania University was founded by Mir Osman Ali Khan in 1917–18, not 1930; the other dates are correct.

nindian-history-108-14.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sir William Jones – Asiatic Society of Bengal, 1784
nindian-history-108-14.x: William Jones founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784; Hastings founded the Calcutta Madrasa (1781), Macaulay wrote the 1835 Minute and Charles Wood sent the 1854 Despatch.

nindian-history-124-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Hunter Commission of 1882?
o: It was associated with W.W. Hunter.
nindian-history-124-2.x: Famine policy was the work of the Strachey Commission; the Hunter Commission under W.W. Hunter dealt with education.

nindian-history-124-12.s: Who chaired the Royal Commission on Agriculture (1926)?
nindian-history-124-12.x: Lord Linlithgow chaired the Royal Commission on Agriculture in 1926; Butler, Hunter and Lee headed other inquiries.

nindian-history-124-17.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Campbell Commission inquired into the Orissa famine.
2. The Royal Commission on Agriculture dealt with constitutional reforms.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
nindian-history-124-17.x: Only 1 is correct: the Campbell Commission inquired into the 1866 Orissa famine, while the Royal Commission on Agriculture dealt with agriculture, not constitutional reforms.

nindian-history-135-10.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First railway line in Eastern India – Bombay–Thane
Starting point of the first railway – Thane
First railway line in North India – Delhi–Agra
nindian-history-135-10.x: The first line in North India was Delhi–Agra; the first railway ran Bombay–Thane from Bori Bunder, and the first in Eastern India was Howrah–Hooghly.

n10f0b4fa169.s: The English newspaper Justice was edited by:
n10f0b4fa169.x: Justice was an English newspaper edited by T.M. Nair.

na244fbb193b.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
na244fbb193b.x: The Famine Code was issued in 1883; Wood's Despatch was 1854, the First Factory Act 1881 and the Resolution on Local Self-Government 1882.

nf43de5441c1.s: The Indian Civil Services Act of 1861 allowed limited Indian entry mainly into:
nf43de5441c1.x: The 1861 Act allowed limited Indian entry, mainly into uncovenanted posts, subject to conditions such as seven years' residence and a local-language examination.

n7822c180484.s: Simultaneous ICS examinations in India and England, held from 1922, were provided for by the:
n7822c180484.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for a separate ICS examination in India, held from 1922 alongside the London examination.

nindian-history-107-4.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nindian-history-107-4.x: The Aitchison Commission sat in 1886/87; the Macaulay Committee was 1854, the Lee Commission 1924 and the Federal and Provincial PSCs 1935.

nee8619ffc04.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Father of Modern Western Education in India – Lord Dalhousie
Father of Civil Services in India – Lord Wellesley
Father of Civil Services in India – Lord Cornwallis
nee8619ffc04.x: Lord Cornwallis is the Father of Civil Services in India; Wellesley was the Bengal Tiger and Bentinck is linked with modern Western education.

nc01781248fd.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nc01781248fd.x: The Indian Penal Code dates from 1860; the Code of Civil Procedure from 1859 and the Code of Criminal Procedure from 1861.

nindian-history-134-20.s: Under the Indian High Courts Act of 1861, the High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were set up in:
nindian-history-134-20.x: The High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were set up in 1862; Allahabad followed in 1866.

n08b7756d1b6.s: Besides financial decentralisation, Lord Mayo's administration is associated with:
o: a statistical survey of India and the first census
the first municipal corporation at Madras
the transfer of local self-government to the provinces
n08b7756d1b6.x: Lord Mayo undertook a statistical survey of India and conducted the first census (1871).

nindian-history-26-2-31.s: Which of the following pairs (centre of 1857 – leader) is correctly matched?
nindian-history-26-2-31.x: Begum Hazrat Mahal led at Lucknow; Bahadur Shah II led at Delhi, Nana Sahib at Kanpur and Kunwar Singh at Jagdishpur.

nindian-history-26-2-39.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Jagdishpur was located in Bihar.
2. Khan Bahadur Khan led the Revolt of 1857 at Bareilly.
3. Khan Bahadur Khan led the Revolt of 1857 at Jagdishpur.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-history-26-2-39.x: 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because Jagdishpur was led by Kunwar Singh.

nindian-history-121-5.s: Who was the military commander who fought on behalf of Nana Sahib at Kanpur in 1857?
nindian-history-121-5.x: Tatya Tope was the military commander at Kanpur fighting for Nana Sahib, the political leader there.

nindian-history-6-8.s: Which of the following pairs (book – author) is correctly matched?
o: India Wins Freedom – Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
The Story of the Integration of the Indian States – Subhas Chandra Bose
nindian-history-6-8.x: India Wins Freedom is by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad; India Divided is by Rajendra Prasad, The Indian Struggle by Subhas Chandra Bose and the integration book by V.P. Menon.

nindian-history-6-28.s: Which of the following pairs (book – author) is correctly matched?
o: New Dimensions of India's Foreign Policy – P.V. Narasimha Rao
The Foundations of Indian Culture – Atal Bihari Vajpayee
nindian-history-6-28.x: Living an Era is by D.P. Mishra; the foreign-policy book is Vajpayee's, The Foundations of Indian Culture is Sri Aurobindo's and Ayodhya: 6 December 1992 is P.V. Narasimha Rao's.

nindian-history-6-22.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Nation in Making was written by S.N. Banerjee.
2. Towards Struggle was written by Jayaprakash Narayan.
3. India Wins Freedom was written by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
Which of the above statements are correct?

nindian-history-6-25.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Problems of the Far East was written by George N. Curzon.
2. The Untold Story was written by Brijmohan Kaul.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
nindian-history-6-25.x: Both are correct: Lord Curzon wrote Problems of the Far East and Lt Gen B.M. Kaul wrote The Untold Story.

n89c41cd6340.s: After entering the Red Fort in May 1857, the rebels at Delhi killed:
n89c41cd6340.x: After reaching Delhi, the rebels entered the Red Fort and killed Commissioner Simon Fraser.

nd1ade1bbc1c.s: Which of the following pairs (leader of 1857 – centre) is correctly matched?
nd1ade1bbc1c.x: Kunwar Singh led at Arrah (Bihar); Hazrat Mahal led at Lucknow, Nana Saheb at Kanpur and Bahadur Shah Zafar at Delhi.

n77b2159f971.s:
With reference to Hyderabad during the Revolt of 1857, consider the following statements:
1. Mubariz-ud-Daula's imprisonment in Golconda came before Turrebaz Khan's attack on the Residency.
2. Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula joined the rebels against the British.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
n77b2159f971.x: Only 1 is correct: Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned before Turrebaz Khan's attack; the Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula stayed pro-British.

nindian-history-120-26.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Birsa Munda was associated with the Munda Ulgulan.
2. Sidhu and Kanhu were associated with the Santhal Rebellion.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
nindian-history-120-26.x: Both are correct: Birsa Munda led the Ulgulan of 1899–1900 and Sidhu and Kanhu led the Santhal Rebellion of 1855–56.

na6e2ec5ff6a.s: The East India Company, whose political rule ended under the Act of 1858, was formally dissolved in:
na6e2ec5ff6a.x: The Government of India Act, 1858 ended the Company's political rule, and the Company was formally dissolved in 1874.

n0f4e7fa172d.s: Queen Victoria, given the title 'Empress of India' by the Royal Titles Act 1876, was proclaimed so at the Delhi Durbar in:
n0f4e7fa172d.x: The title was proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar of 1 January 1877 under Lord Lytton.

n96eeb83a09f.s: The Treaty of Aurangabad of 1753, part of the background to the Battle of Bobbili, gave the Circars to the:
n96eeb83a09f.x: The Treaty of Aurangabad of 1753 gave the Circars to the French.

na11724e959e.s: Which of the following pairs (place/person – nature of resistance) is correctly matched?
o: Kurnool – resistance led by French officers
Parlakimedi – revolt by the Nizam's army
Ghumsur – resistance by zamindars against the Company
Bhupayya – resistance confined to the Madras Presidency
na11724e959e.x: The zamindars of Ghumsur (and Parlakimedi) in Ganjam resisted the Company; Kurnool had no French role and Parlakimedi's resistance was by zamindars, not the Nizam's army.

nap-history-12-2.s: Which of the following pairs (battle – year) is correctly matched?
nap-history-12-2.x: Padmanabham was fought in 1794; Bobbili was 1757, Chandurthi 1758 and Raichur 1520.

nap-history-12-5.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Battle of Palnadu, Nagamma and Nalagama Raju were responsible, and Kakati Rudra Deva helped.
2. The Muthukur Battle was fought between Ganapatideva's Kakatiyas, allied with Manmasiddhi II, and the Pandyan king Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

nap-history-12-21.s: Which of the following pairs (battle – alternative name) is correctly matched?
o: Battle of Bobbili – Battle of Padmanabha
Battle of Padmanabham – Battle of Palanadu
Battle of Tallikota – Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi
nap-history-12-21.x: Tallikota is also called the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi; Bobbili is the Bobbili-Vizianagaram battle, Padmanabham the Battle of Padmanabha and Palnadu the Battle of Palanadu.

naf4cdac5d39.s: Which group formed the support base of Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's revolt?
o: Only officials from the Godavari Agency
Farmers, Yanadis, tribal people and people of the Uyyalawada and Nosam estates
Only zamindars from Parlakimedi and Ghumsur
Sepoys of the Madras Army alone
naf4cdac5d39.x: The movement had about 5,000 followers, including farmers, Yanadis, tribal people and people from the Uyyalawada and Nosam estates.

na1287bd13bd.s: Orvakal airport in Kurnool, operational from 25 March 2021, has been named after:
na1287bd13bd.x: Orvakal airport was renamed Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport.

nf9a5d324eaf.s: After the 2022 district reorganisation, Uyyalawada is located in:
nf9a5d324eaf.x: After the 2022 reorganisation, Uyyalawada falls in Nandyal district.

nf9fbb1051b5.s: Who succeeded Nizam Nasir-ud-Daula in Hyderabad in 1857?
nf9fbb1051b5.x: Afzal-ud-Daula succeeded Nasir-ud-Daula in 1857 and ruled until 1869.

n34acddf84b0.s: As a reward for loyalty after 1857, which territories were restored to Hyderabad, along with the writing off of its debt?
n34acddf84b0.x: The Raichur Doab and Dharashiv were restored to Hyderabad and its debt was written off.

ncb7483c43dc.s: Which of the following pairs (leader – place or event of 1857) is correctly matched?
o: Turrebaz Khan – Attack on the British Residency
Korukonda Subba Reddy – Imprisoned in Golconda Fort
ncb7483c43dc.x: Turrebaz Khan attacked the British Residency; Dandasena rose at Paralakimidi, Subba Reddy led at Errannagudem and Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned in Golconda Fort.
